entities.description: Anarchism is a political philosophy and movement that is skeptical of all justifications for authority and seeks to abolish the state and other involuntary coercive institutions.
The Enlightenment was an intellectual and philosophical movement that dominated the world of ideas in Europe during the 18th century, the 'Century of Philosophy'.
The Paris Commune was a revolutionary socialist government that ruled Paris from 18 March to 28 May 1871, establishing socialist policies and defying the French national government.
The Russian Civil War was a multi-party civil war in the former Russian Empire immediately following the Russian Revolutions of 1917, as many factions vied to determine Russia's political future.
The Spanish Civil War was a civil war in Spain fought from 1936 to 1939 between the Republicans and the Nationalists, led by General Francisco Franco.
Ancient Greek refers to the Greek language from the archaic period to the end of antiquity, spoken across the ancient Greek world.
William Godwin was an English journalist, political philosopher, novelist, and abolitionist who is considered one of the first exponents of anarchism.
Wilhelm Weitling was a German tailor, inventor, and social theorist who became one of the first German communists and an early theoretician of anarchism.
Pierre-Joseph Proudhon was a French socialist, philosopher, economist, and mutualist who was the first person to declare himself an anarchist.
France is a country in Western Europe, known for its history, culture, and influence on political thought.
The United States is a country primarily located in North America, a major global power and a significant site of anarchist thought and movements.
The New Left was a broad political movement mainly in the 1960s and 1970s that sought a broader definition of political activism, including civil rights, feminism, and anti-war movements.
Marxists are adherents of the theories of Karl Marx, emphasizing class struggle, historical materialism, and the eventual overthrow of capitalism.

A socialist is a person who advocates or practices socialism, a political and economic theory of social organization which advocates that the means of production, distribution, and exchange should be owned or regulated by the community as a whole.
China is a large East Asian country with a long history and diverse philosophical traditions, including Taoism.
Taoist philosophers are thinkers who developed and espoused the principles of Taoism, an ancient Chinese philosophy and religion emphasizing living in harmony with the Tao.
Zhuang Zhou, commonly known as Zhuangzi, was an influential Chinese philosopher who lived around the 4th century BC during the Warring States period, contributing significantly to Taoism.
Laozi was an ancient Chinese philosopher and writer, traditionally regarded as the author of the Tao Te Ching and the founder of philosophical Taoism.
Stoicism is an ancient Greek school of philosophy founded at Athens by Zeno of Citium, teaching that virtue, reason, and living in agreement with nature are the highest good.
Greece is a country in Southeast Europe, considered the cradle of Western civilization and philosophy.
Aeschylus was an ancient Greek tragedian, often described as the father of tragedy.
Sophocles was an ancient Greek tragedian, one of the three ancient Greek tragedians whose plays have survived.
The myth of Antigone is an ancient Greek tragedy written by Sophocles, exploring themes of law, conscience, and individual defiance.
Socrates was a classical Greek philosopher credited as one of the founders of Western philosophy.
Athenian authorities refer to the governing bodies and officials of ancient Athens, responsible for maintaining law and order.
Cynics were a group of ancient Greek philosophers who advocated living in accordance with nature, rejecting conventional desires for wealth, power, and fame.
Stoics were adherents of Stoicism, an ancient Greek school of philosophy that taught the development of self-control and fortitude as a means of overcoming destructive emotions.
Europe is a continent located entirely in the Northern Hemisphere and mostly in the Eastern Hemisphere, a historical center of political and philosophical developments.
Muslim movements refer to various social, political, or religious groups and initiatives within Islamic communities throughout history.
The Sasanian Empire was the last Iranian empire before the early Muslim conquests of the 7th century AD, ruling from 224 to 651 AD.
Mazdak was a Zoroastrian prophet and social reformer who gained influence during the reign of the Sasanian king Kavadh I, advocating for communal property and social justice.
Emperor Kavad I was the Sasanian King of Kings of Iran from 488 to 531, who supported the Mazdakite movement during his reign.
Basra is an Iraqi city located on the Shatt al-Arab river, historically a significant center of learning and culture in the Islamic world.
The Renaissance was a period in European history marking the transition from the Middle Ages to modernity, covering the 15th and 16th centuries, characterized by a resurgence of art and learning.
The Reformation was a major movement within Western Christianity in 16th-century Europe that posed a religious and political challenge to the Catholic Church.

The French Revolution was a period of far-reaching social and political upheaval in France and its colonies beginning in 1789, leading to the overthrow of the monarchy and the establishment of a republic.
The Enragés were a small number of radical activists who played an active part in the French Revolution, arguing for direct democracy and economic equality.
Max Stirner was a German philosopher, one of the first thinkers of anarchism, whose work 'The Ego and Its Own' is a founding text of individualist anarchism.
England is a country that is part of the United Kingdom, historically a birthplace of influential political philosophies and movements.
Mutualism is an anarchist school of thought and economic theory that advocates for a society where individuals or groups might exchange products of their labor based on mutually agreed contracts.
Mikhail Bakunin was a Russian revolutionary anarchist, and a founder of collectivist anarchism, who played a significant role in the First International.

The International Workingmen's Association, often called the First International, was an international organization which aimed at uniting a variety of left-wing socialist, communist and anarchist groups and trade unions.
The First International was an international organization which aimed at uniting a variety of left-wing socialist, communist and anarchist groups and trade unions.
Karl Marx was a German philosopher, economist, historian, sociologist, political theorist, journalist, and socialist revolutionary whose ideas formed the basis of Marxism.
The General Council was the leading body of the International Workingmen's Association, which played a central role in its political direction.
The Jura Federation was a section of the International Workingmen's Association (First International) in Switzerland, known for its anarchist tendencies and opposition to the General Council.
Proudhon refers to Pierre-Joseph Proudhon, a French socialist, philosopher, economist, and mutualist who was the first person to declare himself an anarchist.
Bakuninists were followers of Mikhail Bakunin, advocating for collectivist anarchism and revolutionary action.
The 1872 Hague Congress was a meeting of the First International where a major schism occurred between the followers of Karl Marx and Mikhail Bakunin.
The Second International was an organization of socialist and labor parties formed in 1889, lasting until 1916, that continued the work of the dissolved First International.
The St. Imier International was an anarchist international formed in 1872 by various anarchist federations that were expelled or withdrew from the First International.
Peter Kropotkin was a Russian anarchist, socialist, revolutionary, economist, historian, writer, and prominent proponent of anarcho-communism.
Russian refers to anything related to Russia, its people, language, or culture, particularly in the context of revolutionary movements.

Anarcho-communism is a political philosophy and anarchist school of thought that advocates for a stateless society with common ownership of the means of production, direct democracy, and a horizontal network of voluntary associations.
Tokyo is the capital and largest city of Japan, and a major global economic and cultural center.
East Asian countries refer to the nations located in the eastern part of Asia, including China, Japan, and Korea, with diverse political and social histories.
Latin America is a group of countries and dependencies in the Americas where Romance languages are predominantly spoken, with a rich history of social and political movements.
Argentina is a South American country, known for its significant anarchist movements and labor struggles in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

Anarcho-syndicalism is a theory of anarchism that views revolutionary industrial unionism or syndicalism as a method for workers in capitalist society to gain control of an economy and, with that, control of society at large.
Propaganda of the deed refers to provocative actions performed to incite revolution, popular in anarchist circles in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
The Immigration Act of 1903, also known as the Anarchist Exclusion Act, was a United States federal law that prohibited the entry of anarchists and other political radicals into the country.
The Anarchist Exclusion Act was a United States federal law that prohibited the entry of anarchists and other political radicals into the country.
Illegalism is an anarchist philosophy that developed primarily in France, Italy, Belgium, and Switzerland during the early 20th century, which openly embraced criminality as a lifestyle.
The Russian Revolution was a period of political and social revolution that took place in the former Russian Empire which commenced with the abolition of the monarchy in 1917.
The White movement was a loose confederation of anti-communist forces that fought the Bolsheviks in the Russian Civil War.
The Makhnovshchina was an attempt to establish a stateless anarchist society in parts of Ukraine during the Russian Revolution, led by Nestor Makhno.
The Bolshevik government refers to the government established by the Bolshevik party in Russia after the October Revolution, which led to the formation of the Soviet Union.
The Kronstadt rebellion was an unsuccessful uprising by Russian sailors, soldiers, and civilians against the Bolshevik government in March 1921, during the later years of the Russian Civil War.
Petrograd was the name of St. Petersburg from 1914 to 1924, a major city in Russia and a center of revolutionary activity.
Moscow is the capital and largest city of Russia, a historical and political center.
Ukraine is a country in Eastern Europe, significant in anarchist history due to the Makhnovshchina movement.
Platformism is a tendency within the anarchist movement that stresses the need for tightly organized anarchist federations with a unified political program.

Synthesis Anarchism is a form of anarchism that attempts to reconcile different anarchist currents, such as anarcho-communism, anarcho-syndicalism, and individualist anarchism, into one cohesive movement.
The October Revolution was a revolution in Russia led by the Bolshevik Party of Vladimir Lenin that was a key event in the Russian Revolution of 1917.
The General Confederation of Labour (CGT) is a national trade union center in France, historically associated with anarcho-syndicalism.

entities.canonical_name: the Industrial Workers of the World
entities.description: The Industrial Workers of the World (IWW) is an international labor union founded in 1905 in Chicago, known for its radical, anti-capitalist, and anarcho-syndicalist principles.
The Communist International, also known as the Third International, was an international organization founded in 1919 that advocated world communism.
The Spanish Civil War of 1936–39 was a civil war in Spain fought from 1936 to 1939 between the Republicans and the Nationalists, with significant anarchist participation.
The CNT (Confederación Nacional del Trabajo) is a Spanish anarcho-syndicalist trade union, historically one of the most significant forces during the Spanish Civil War.
The FAI (Federación Anarquista Ibérica) is an Iberian Anarchist Federation, a Spanish anarchist organization that was closely associated with the CNT during the Spanish Civil War.
Joseph Stalin was a Georgian revolutionary and Soviet political leader who governed the Soviet Union from the mid-1920s until his death in 1953.
The Soviet Union was a socialist state that existed from 1922 to 1991, centered in Eurasia, which played a significant role in 20th-century global politics.
A Republican government is a form of government in which a state is ruled by representatives of the citizen body, usually established after the overthrow of a monarchy or other non-republican system.
The May Days refer to a series of clashes in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain, between 3 and 8 May 1937, during the Spanish Civil War, between various factions.
World War II was a global war that lasted from 1939 to 1945, involving the vast majority of the world's countries and profoundly impacting global politics.
Marxism–Leninism is a communist ideology and the main communist movement in the 20th century, which became the official state ideology of the Soviet Union.
The Cold War was a period of geopolitical rivalry between the United States and its allies on one side, and the Soviet Union and its allies on the other, from the mid-1940s until the early 1990s.
Anti-nuclear movements are social movements that oppose nuclear weapons, nuclear power, or both.
Environmental movements are social movements that advocate for the protection of the environment and sustainable living.
Peace movements are social movements that seek to achieve ideals such as the ending of a particular war, minimize inter-human violence, and promote pacifism.
The counterculture of the 1960s was an anti-establishment cultural phenomenon that developed primarily in the United States and the United Kingdom, before spreading to much of the Western world.
Crass was an English punk rock band formed in 1977, known for promoting anarchism, environmentalism, and animal rights.
The Sex Pistols were an English punk rock band formed in London in 1975, credited with initiating the punk movement in the United Kingdom.

Anarcha-feminism is a political philosophy that combines anarchism with feminism, viewing patriarchy as a manifestation of involuntary hierarchy that should be opposed alongside the state and capitalism.
Black anarchism is an anarchist school of thought that emphasizes both anarchism and racial justice, focusing on dismantling white supremacy and state oppression affecting Black communities.
Eurocentric demographic refers to population groups primarily originating from or culturally influenced by Europe.
Northern Europe is the northern part or region of Europe, encompassing various countries with distinct histories and cultures.
The World Trade Organization (WTO) is an intergovernmental organization that regulates and facilitates international trade.
The Group of Eight (G8) was an intergovernmental political forum from 1997 until 2014, composed of the then-eight leading industrial nations.

The World Economic Forum is an international non-governmental and lobbying organisation, committed to improving the state of the world by engaging business, political, academic, and other leaders to shape global, regional, and industry agendas.

Black blocs are a tactic used by protesters, consisting of a group of individuals wearing black clothing, ski masks, scarves, sunglasses, or other garments to conceal their identities and avoid criminal prosecution.
The Internet is a global computer network providing a variety of information and communication facilities, consisting of interconnected networks using standardized communication protocols.
The 1999 Seattle WTO conference was a meeting of the World Trade Organization in Seattle, Washington, that was met with large-scale protests and direct action.
The Zapatistas are a left-wing revolutionary political and militant group based in Chiapas, Mexico, that advocates for indigenous rights and autonomy.
Mexico is a country in the southern portion of North America, known for its indigenous cultures and revolutionary movements.

entities.canonical_name: the Democratic Federation of Northern Syria
entities.description: The Democratic Federation of Northern Syria, also known as Rojava, is a de facto autonomous region in northeastern Syria, governed on principles of democratic confederalism.
Rojava is a de facto autonomous region in northeastern Syria, governed on principles of democratic confederalism, with strong influences from anarchist and libertarian socialist thought.
Syria is a country in Western Asia, which has recently seen the emergence of autonomous regions with anarchist-influenced governance models.
Carissa Honeywell is a contemporary scholar and writer on anarchism, known for her contributions to anarchist theory and history.
Food not Bombs is a loose-knit collective of independent chapters, sharing free vegan meals with the hungry and protesting war and poverty.
Monsanto was an American agrochemical and agricultural biotechnology corporation, often a target of anti-corporate and environmental protests.
Social anarchism is a branch of anarchism that sees individual freedom as being connected with social equality and emphasizes community and mutual aid.
Individualist anarchism is a political philosophy that advocates for the individual over external social or political structures and emphasizes individual liberty and autonomy.
Green anarchism is a school of thought within anarchism that emphasizes environmentalism, seeing anarchism as the logical extension of ecological concerns.
Post-anarchism is a theoretical current that combines classical anarchist theory with post-structuralist and postmodern thought.

Philosophical anarchism is an anarchist school of thought that contends that the state lacks moral legitimacy and that individuals have no moral obligation to obey state law, but does not necessarily advocate revolution to eliminate the state.
Anarcho-capitalism is a political philosophy and economic theory that advocates the elimination of the state in favor of individual sovereignty in a free market.

Bolshevism was a revolutionary Marxist current of political thought and political movement associated with the formation of a rigidly centralized, cohesive and disciplined party of social revolution, focused on overthrowing existing capitalist state power.
Feudalism was a social system in medieval Europe in which land was exchanged for service or labor.

Fundamentalist Islam refers to various religious movements advocating a return to what adherents believe are the fundamental principles of Islam, often characterized by strict adherence to religious texts and laws.
Roman Catholicism is the largest Christian church, led by the Pope in Rome, and has played a significant role in European history and culture.
Patriarchy is a social system in which men hold primary power and predominate in roles of political leadership, moral authority, social privilege, and control of property.
Heterosexism is a system of attitudes, bias, and discrimination in favor of opposite-sex sexuality and relationships.
White supremacy is the belief that white people are superior to people of other races and therefore should dominate society.
Imperialism is a policy or ideology of extending a country's rule over foreign nations, often by military force or by gaining political and economic control.
